All four variations the JR papers print reproduce at the paper's rounding. A fifth, in the
authors' repository, uses a lower tax rate, which cannot be set in this OPA. None of the five
changes a single assumption, so the papers give no printed check of the explorer's one-input
settings.

## What was checked

The main estimate of the JR analysis is a mean net present value of −$38.9 billion (NBER chapter,
September 2026, p.35). This OPA computes it as −$38.98 billion exactly, and as −$38.89 billion
with the authors' random seed. The September chapter prints no net present value under other
assumptions. The first version (SSRN, March 2026) prints four, and the authors' public repository
holds one more. Each check below sets the same assumptions in this OPA and compares the result
with the printed figure.

Each of the five changes two or more inputs at once from the main estimate. The first version's
Monte Carlo changes the revenue range and the rule for the share of income tax lost. Each
scenario of its Table 9 fixes four inputs at single values.

## Results

All figures are net present values in billions of dollars. Table 9 prints three values per
scenario, one for each discount rate (1.5%, 3% and 4.5%). "Match" means this OPA's value rounds to
the printed figure.

| Variation | Source | Printed | This OPA | Result | How to set it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main assumptions, for reference | NBER, p.35 | −38.9 | −38.98 (seeded run −38.89) | Match | Explorer, as it opens |
| Revenue drawn from $35B to $67.51B, and the share lost tied to the revenue (f = 1 − revenue / 94.2) | SSRN, p.20 | −24.7 | −24.71 | Match | Explorer: Jump to "First version, March 2026" |
| Six departures: revenue $67.51B, income tax $3.3B a year, share lost 28.3% | SSRN, Table 9 | +5.2 / +36.3 / +46.7 | +5.18 / +36.34 / +46.73 | Match | R code |
| Central: revenue $42.0B, income tax $4.55B a year, share lost 55.4% | SSRN, Table 9 | −126.1 / −42.0 / −14.0 | −126.09 / −42.04 / −14.03 | Match | R code |
| Literature calibrated: revenue $35.0B, income tax $5.8B a year, share lost 62.8% | SSRN, Table 9 | −208.0 / −86.5 / −46.0 | −208.00 / −86.50 / −46.00 | Match | R code |
| Tax rate 2% instead of 5%, central inputs, 3% discount rate | Authors' repository, a plot | −67.2 | none | Cannot be set | None |

## What could not be checked

**The tax rate.** This OPA has no setting for a wealth tax rate other than 5%. The repository's 2%
case is reproduced only by building its inputs by hand (−67.22).

**The explorer's one-input settings.** The explorer offers "Rate 1.5%", "Rate 4.5%" and
"Litigation weight q = 0.5", each of which changes one input from the main estimate. The authors
print no net present value for any of them.

## Who ran these checks

Claude Code agents chose the variations from the papers and ran the checks on 15 October 2026.
The scripts were then rerun once, in a separate session, with the same results. The author has
not yet reviewed these checks.

To rerun them from the repository root, with a clone of the authors' repository:

```sh
export RAUH_REPO_DIR=<path to the authors' repository>
Rscript feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr-sensitivity.R
```

The full record, with the source of every figure, is in
[jr-sensitivity.md](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr-sensitivity.md).
A second record, [jr.md](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/jr.md),
checks ten other numbers the papers print. All reproduce except the chapter's "expanded
departures" (Table 8, about 42% of the base), which no grouping of the authors' departure records
gives.

## Settings the papers do not print

This OPA lets a reader change assumptions the papers hold fixed. The table below lists ten such
changes, each made one at a time from the September chapter's main assumptions, with the result
this OPA gives. The papers print no figure for any of them, so they are untested against the
authors' own work.

We have sent this table to the original authors, requesting them to test whether they obtain the
same results. We will update the responses here.

The mean net present value is in billions of dollars. This OPA computes the exact average of the
authors' formula over the same random draws, not a new seeded run. A seeded run of the authors'
script differs from it by sampling error only (at the main setting, −38.89 against −38.98). Each setting can be made
in the [explorer](explorer/).

| Setting changed from the main assumptions | Mean net present value | Share of runs below zero | Authors' result |
|---|---|---|---|
| None, the main assumptions, for reference | −38.98 | 85.3% | |
| Discount rate fixed at 1.5% (instead of drawn from 1.5% to 4.5%) | −100.50 | 100.0% | Pending |
| Discount rate fixed at 4.5% | −9.50 | 63.2% | Pending |
| Revenue multiplied by a chance of surviving in court of 0.75 | −47.98 | 94.6% | Pending |
| Revenue multiplied by a chance of surviving in court of 0.50 | −56.98 | 99.5% | Pending |
| Yearly income tax fixed at $3.3B (instead of drawn from $3.3B to $5.8B) | −18.38 | 71.1% | Pending |
| Yearly income tax fixed at $5.8B | −59.58 | 94.7% | Pending |
| Lost income tax grows 0.5% a year (instead of not growing) | −58.62 | 90.9% | Pending |
| Lost income tax grows 1% a year | −96.81 | 95.1% | Pending |
| Lowest revenue the draw can pick of $35B (instead of $0) | −21.48 | 71.8% | Pending |
| Share of the income tax base that leaves fixed at 0.283 (instead of drawn from 0.30 to 0.60) | −11.21 | 64.0% | Pending |

The values are read from the explorer's own data file, `site/explorer/grid.js`, which the
pipeline writes.
